notes: 1. SM portal login URL is the BARE path https://uat-web.xrportal.in/sales-manager (NOT /sales-manager/login). The unrelated /login page is the Growth-Partner / Channel-Partner login — a different portal entry point (see visual-memory sm/login INDEX.md Route section).

2. SM auth is Mobile-OTP only (no password). Step 1 = mobile entry + role selection, Step 2 = 6-box OTP entry. Successful verify redirects to /sales-manager/callback-requests (NOT a dashboard/home). JWT session is stateless and lasts ~1 day.

3. Role selector: an Ant Design Radio.Group (name="role") with two options — 'Sales Manager Admin' (value sales_manager_admin, the DEFAULT selection) and 'Sales Manager' (value sales_manager). Lookup is scoped to roleId IN (4,5); the role chosen on screen is sent in the send-otp/verify-otp payload and must match the user's actual role or the lookup fails with 'User not found'.

4. SM master OTP = 258369 (this is ADMIN_MASTER_OTP, NOT the regular masterOtp); UAT SM mobile = 8888888888. The master OTP works for any registered SM mobile on UAT and bypasses real SMS delivery, in all environments.

5. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT account/state must be supplied before executing this test (e.g. an isActive=false SM user, an unregistered mobile, an Admin-only-role mobile, an aged/short-expiry JWT, or a valid API bearer token / API client).
6. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

7. SECURITY GAPS (documented, shared with Admin auth.controller — SM uses the same backend): No backend OTP rate limit / cooldown — the 60s re-send gate is UI-only (FS 1.5 Rule 3, auth.controller.js:558-568 commented out). No wrong-OTP lockout. Logout is a client-side clear only — the JWT stays valid server-side until natural ~1-day expiry (do NOT write a post-logout 401 pass case). OTP is generated with Math.random() and stored plaintext. Master OTP has no production gate.

8. NOTIFICATION CHANNEL: OTP SMS is delivered via Epinet (NOT Kaleyra). Kaleyra is used for WhatsApp/click-to-call notifications to customers, never for OTP (BRD §7, FS 1.6.1, FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25). OTP verification itself dispatches NO SMS/WhatsApp/email (silent by design).

9. DOC_DRIFT-001 — send-otp/verify-otp request body uses field `phone` (with countryCode '+91' and role), per visual-memory INDEX.md Redux actions (sendSalesManagerOtp / verifySalesManagerOtp). The verify response wraps the JWT as response.data.token with a user object. Live implementation wins over any stale BRD/FRD example; TCs in this pass use the observed `phone`/wrapped-token shape.

10. GLOSSARY: 'Send OTP' = button.ant-btn-submit on Step 1; 'Submit OTP' = button.ant-btn-submit on Step 2; 'Re-Send OTP' = button.common-link on the OTP screen; Back = the chevron-left button.reset-btn.back-to-mobile. Success toasts (antd .ant-message-notice, top-center): 'OTP sent successfully!' on send, 'Login successful! Redirecting...' on verify.

tcs.scenario: To verify the SM login page loads at /sales-manager
tcs.description: Verify that the Sales Manager login page renders correctly when the browser opens the bare /sales-manager path with no active session.
tcs.precond: Browser is open with no active SM session (any stale tokens are wiped on entering the route).
tcs.steps:
1. Go to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/sales-manager.
2. Wait for the page to finish loading.
tcs.expected: The SM login page renders within about 5 seconds showing the brand logo, the 'Sales Manager Login' heading, the mobile number field, the role selector and the Send OTP button. (Page title 'HoABL | Sales Manager'.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the page title and form on first load
tcs.description: Verify that loading /sales-manager shows the correct page title and the Step-1 form, and that stale tokens are cleared on entry.
tcs.precond: Browser open at 1920x900 with no active session.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/sales-manager.
2. Read the browser tab title and observe the rendered form.
tcs.expected: Browser tab title reads 'HoABL | Sales Manager'. The heading 'SALES MANAGER LOGIN' is shown, with the mobile field, role selector and Send OTP button below it. Any stale auth tokens are cleared on entering the route.

tcs.scenario: To verify all static elements on the mobile screen

tcs.precond: The SM login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:

2. Note each visible element.
tcs.expected: The page shows: brand logo, 'Sales Manager Login' heading, the role selector with 'Sales Manager Admin' and 'Sales Manager' options, a '+91' prefix, the mobile field with placeholder 'Enter Mobile Number', the Send OTP button, and an error area (hidden by default).

tcs.scenario: To verify the brand logo and portal title render

tcs.steps:
1. Look at the header/logo area above the form.
2. Confirm the logo image loads and the portal identifier text is visible.
tcs.expected: The brand logo image renders fully (no broken-image icon / no 404) and a 'Sales Manager' portal identifier is visible above the form.

tcs.scenario: To verify Send OTP with a valid registered SM mobile

2. Click Send OTP.

tcs.scenario: To verify Send OTP transitions to the OTP screen

tcs.scenario: To verify Send OTP is blocked with an empty mobile

tcs.steps:
1. Leave the mobile field empty.
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: Send OTP stays disabled or a validation error 'Please enter a valid 10-digit mobile number' is shown; no OTP request is fired and the page stays on Step 1.

tcs.scenario: To verify empty mobile submission blocks Send OTP
tcs.description: Verify that submitting an empty mobile field triggers a required/invalid validation and fires no API call.
tcs.precond: The SM login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Leave the mobile field empty.
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: A field-level error indicates the mobile is required / invalid; no send-otp API call is fired.

tcs.scenario: To verify a mobile shorter than 10 digits is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that a 9-digit mobile is treated as invalid and no OTP is sent.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter '888888888' (9 digits).
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: A validation error 'Please enter a valid 10-digit mobile number' is shown and the OTP is not sent.

tcs.scenario: To verify a too-short mobile shows a validation error
tcs.description: Verify that a clearly short value blocks OTP dispatch with the inline error.
tcs.precond: The SM login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Type '12345' in the mobile field.
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: Inline validation error 'Please enter a valid 10-digit mobile number' is shown; no OTP is dispatched and the form stays on the mobile screen.

tcs.scenario: To verify a mobile longer than 10 digits is capped/rejected
tcs.description: Verify that typing more than 10 digits is truncated or rejected so no over-length mobile is sent.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Try typing '88888888888' (11 digits).
2. Read the field value.
3. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: The field truncates to the first 10 digits; the OTP request is fired only for the 10-digit value (no over-length payload).

tcs.scenario: To verify the mobile field rejects non-numeric characters
tcs.description: Verify that letters and special characters cannot be entered into the mobile field.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the mobile field.
2. Try typing letters, then special characters like @ # $.
3. Try pasting 'abcdefghij'.
tcs.expected: The field accepts digits only; letters and special characters are blocked or stripped on entry.

tcs.scenario: To verify non-numeric mobile fails validation
tcs.description: Verify that a non-numeric mobile, if forced, fails the phone-format validation.
tcs.precond: The SM login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the mobile field.
2. Attempt to type 'abcdefghij' and special characters.
tcs.expected: The telephone input does not accept letters/symbols; if submitted, the phone-format validation fails with 'Please enter a valid 10-digit mobile number'.

tcs.scenario: To verify a mobile not starting with 6-9 is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that an Indian mobile not starting with 6-9 is treated as invalid.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter '5000000000' (starts with 5).
2. Click Send OTP.
3. Repeat with '1234567890' (starts with 1).
tcs.expected: A validation error indicates an invalid Indian mobile and no OTP is fired (Indian mobiles must start with 6-9). [VERIFY WITH DEV] the 6-9 first-digit rule is implied by Indian-mobile format; confirm it is enforced on the SM form.

tcs.scenario: To verify leading zeros and spaces are stripped from the mobile
tcs.description: Verify that surrounding spaces are trimmed and a leading zero is rejected so only a canonical 10-digit number is sent.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Paste '  8888888888  ' (with surrounding spaces).
2. Try entering '08888888888' (leading zero).
3. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: Whitespace is trimmed and the leading zero is rejected; only the canonical 10-digit value '8888888888' is submitted.

tcs.scenario: To verify the mobile field rejects emoji and unicode
tcs.description: Verify that emoji and non-ASCII unicode digits cannot be entered into the mobile field.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Try pasting an emoji into the mobile field.
2. Try pasting Arabic-Indic unicode digits.
3. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: The field rejects emoji and non-ASCII unicode digits; only ASCII 0-9 are accepted, so no malformed payload reaches the backend.

tcs.scenario: To verify an all-zeros mobile is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that an all-zeros 10-digit mobile is rejected at Send OTP.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter '0000000000'.
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: The mobile is rejected (invalid format / not registered); the page stays on the mobile entry screen and no OTP screen loads.

tcs.scenario: To verify a leading-zero 10-digit mobile is treated as unregistered
tcs.description: Verify that a 10-digit mobile starting with 0, if it reaches the backend, is rejected as unregistered.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter '0123456789'.
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: Send OTP does not advance to the OTP screen; the value is rejected at field validation, or if it reaches the backend it returns 'User not found' (no SM record). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm whether the leading-zero value is blocked at the field or rejected at lookup.

tcs.scenario: To verify an unregistered mobile is rejected at Send OTP
tcs.description: Verify that an unregistered mobile is rejected at the send-otp step (not at verify).
tcs.precond: Mobile 7000000099 is NOT registered as an SM in any role. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an unregistered mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter '7000000099'.
2. Click Send OTP.
3. Wait for the response.
tcs.expected: The backend returns 400 'User not found'; the OTP screen does NOT load and the error is shown in the error area.

tcs.scenario: To verify an Admin-role mobile cannot log in at Send OTP
tcs.description: Verify that a user whose only role is Admin (role 1) is rejected at the SM send-otp step because the lookup is scoped to roleId IN (4,5).
tcs.precond: A registered Admin user (role 1) mobile is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an admin-only-role mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the SM login page.
2. Enter the Admin-only mobile.
3. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: The backend returns 400 'User not found' because the SM lookup is scoped to roleId IN (4,5); the Admin cannot enter the SM portal via this page.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Admin role cannot log in via the SM portal
tcs.description: Verify SM/Admin role isolation — an Admin-role user is rejected end-to-end on the SM login page.
tcs.precond: A mobile belonging to an Admin-role-only user is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin-only-role mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /sales-manager.
2. Enter the Admin-only mobile.
3. Send OTP, then enter an OTP and Submit.
tcs.expected: Per FRD §1.2 (Scope) Admin role 1 cannot use this login page; send-otp or verify-otp returns an error and login is rejected — the user stays on the SM login screen.

tcs.scenario: To verify SM-Admin role mismatch is rejected at the auth route
tcs.description: Verify the documented UI/backend coupling: selecting the wrong role tab for an SM-Admin user causes the role-scoped lookup to fail.
tcs.precond: An SM-Admin user (role 4) exists. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an SM-Admin mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. On the mobile screen select the 'Sales Manager' role (sends role 'sales_manager').
2. Enter the SM-Admin's mobile.
3. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: The backend returns 400 'User not found' because the (phone, roleId=5) lookup fails — the SM-Admin is roleId 4. The SM-Admin must select the 'Sales Manager Admin' role to log in (sends role 'sales_manager_admin'). Documents the UI/backend role coupling.

tcs.scenario: To verify login with the Sales Manager (non-admin) role
tcs.description: Verify that selecting the 'Sales Manager' role and logging in succeeds and lands on Callback Requests with role-5 access.
tcs.precond: Mobile 8888888888 is valid for role 5.
tcs.steps:
1. On the mobile screen select the 'Sales Manager' role.
2. Type '8888888888'.
3. Click Send OTP, enter '258369', then Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: The send-otp and verify-otp payloads carry role 'sales_manager'; a JWT is issued reflecting role-5 access and the browser navigates to /sales-manager/callback-requests.

tcs.scenario: To verify the last-selected role is sent in the payload
tcs.description: Verify that switching the role before Send OTP sends the last-selected role, not the prior one.
tcs.precond: The mobile screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Select the 'Sales Manager' role.
2. Switch to the 'Sales Manager Admin' role.
3. Type '8888888888' and click Send OTP.
4. Inspect the send-otp payload (DevTools Network).
tcs.testData: Mobile: 8888888888, role switched to Sales Manager Admin
tcs.expected: The send-otp payload 'role' equals the LAST selected role ('sales_manager_admin'), not the earlier selection, and the same role is echoed in the verify-otp payload.

tcs.scenario: To verify SM-Admin route access vs plain SM
tcs.description: Verify the documented access split: SM-Admin reaches common + admin SM routes; a plain SM is blocked from admin routes.
tcs.precond: A valid SM-Admin JWT (role 4) and a valid SM JWT (role 5) are available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access for both roles.
tcs.steps:
1. As SM-Admin, call a /sales-manager/common/* endpoint, then a /sales-manager/admin/* endpoint.
2. As plain SM (role 5), call a /sales-manager/admin/* endpoint.
tcs.expected: SM-Admin gets 200 on both common and admin routes; the plain SM gets 403 on admin routes (restrictTo('sales_manager_admin')).

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP screen renders six labelled boxes
tcs.description: Verify that the OTP screen shows six single-digit boxes with correct accessibility labels after Send OTP.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown after Send OTP.
tcs.steps:
1. Look at the OTP boxes on the OTP screen.
2. Note their count and labels.
tcs.expected: Six single-digit boxes are rendered, labelled 'OTP Input 1' through 'OTP Input 6'. All boxes are empty on entry and focus auto-advances to the next box as digits are typed.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP screen heading and sub-text
tcs.description: Verify that the OTP screen shows the 'ENTER OTP' heading and the exact helper sub-text.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown after Send OTP.
tcs.steps:
1. Read the heading at the top of the OTP screen.
2. Read the line of text below it.
tcs.expected: The heading reads 'ENTER OTP' and the sub-text reads 'Enter the OTP sent to your phone number'. (Source: visual-memory sm/login Key Structural Notes — OTP screen.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the countdown timer starts and decrements
tcs.description: Verify that the OTP countdown timer starts near 60s and decrements once per second, with Re-Send disabled while it runs.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Observe the timer immediately after Send OTP.
2. Wait about 5 seconds and observe again.
tcs.expected: The timer shows about '60s' on entry (captured as '59s' due to capture latency) and decrements every second; the Re-Send OTP link is disabled while the countdown is active (its text includes 'in NNs').

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP timer starting value
tcs.description: Verify that the countdown timer is visible and starts at its initial value when the OTP screen first appears.
tcs.precond: Send OTP has just been clicked.
tcs.steps: 1. Observe the countdown timer the moment the OTP screen loads.
tcs.expected: The timer is visible and starts at 60s (startTimer(60) per visual-memory notes), shown as '60s'/'59s' depending on render timing. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the canonical start value is not stated in BRD/FRD; confirm 60s is intended.

tcs.scenario: To verify Re-Send OTP is disabled during the timer
tcs.description: Verify that Re-Send OTP cannot be used while the countdown is still running.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown with the timer above 0s.
tcs.steps: 1. While the timer is still counting, look at the Re-Send OTP link and try to click it.
tcs.expected: The Re-Send OTP link is disabled (cannot be clicked) and its text includes an 'in NNs' countdown suffix; no API call can be made during the active timer.

tcs.scenario: To verify Re-Send OTP enables when the timer reaches 0s
tcs.description: Verify that Re-Send OTP becomes enabled once the countdown reaches zero.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown; do not submit; wait the full 60 seconds.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for '8888888888'.
2. Wait until the timer ticks down to '0s'.
3. Look at the Re-Send OTP link.
tcs.expected: When the timer reaches '0s', the Re-Send OTP link becomes enabled, its text is 'Re-Send OTP' (no 'in NNs' suffix) and its styling switches to the active (green/highlighted) state.

tcs.scenario: To verify clicking Re-Send OTP after expiry restarts the flow
tcs.description: Verify that clicking Re-Send OTP after the timer expires dispatches a fresh OTP and restarts the countdown.
tcs.precond: The countdown has reached 0s and Re-Send OTP is enabled.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the enabled 'Re-Send OTP' link.
2. Watch the timer, the boxes and the toast.
tcs.expected: A fresh OTP is requested with the same mobile/role, a success toast 'OTP sent successfully!' appears, the timer restarts at 60s, the OTP boxes reset and Re-Send OTP disables again ('in NNs' suffix returns).

tcs.scenario: To verify Re-Send OTP fires a new send request
tcs.description: Verify that Re-Send OTP fires a fresh send-otp request and lets the user enter the new OTP.
tcs.precond: Send OTP is complete and the OTP screen is shown with Re-Send available.
tcs.steps:
1. Wait for the UI re-send timer to expire.
2. Click Re-Send OTP.
3. Observe the network call and the screen.
tcs.expected: A fresh send-otp request fires, a success toast appears and the user can enter the new OTP. (Note: per FS 1.5 Rule 3 there is no backend rate-limit — the UI timer is the only throttle.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the Back button returns to the mobile screen

tcs.scenario: To verify the full mobile-to-dashboard login flow
tcs.description: Verify the complete SM login journey: mobile, OTP, success toast, storage, websocket, redirect to Callback Requests.
tcs.precond: UAT; mobile 8888888888 registered with an SM role.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /sales-manager.
2. Type '8888888888'.
3. Click Send OTP.
4. On the OTP screen type '258369'.
5. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: A success toast 'Login successful! Redirecting...' appears; localStorage is populated with AUTH_TOKEN, user, permission_check and persist:xanadu_0.0.1; the realtime websocket connects; the browser navigates to /sales-manager/callback-requests and the dashboard renders with 'Welcome, Tester' and the callback requests table.

tcs.scenario: To verify post-login landing is Callback Requests
tcs.description: Verify that a successful login lands on /sales-manager/callback-requests and not the bare /sales-manager route.
tcs.precond: A successful login has completed.
tcs.steps: 1. After verify success, read the URL bar and the rendered module.
tcs.expected: The URL is exactly https://uat-web.xrportal.in/sales-manager/callback-requests (navigate('callback-requests') fires after verify) and the Callback Requests management screen is rendered.

tcs.scenario: To verify the dashboard greeting after login
tcs.description: Verify that after login the dashboard shows the user-context greeting.
tcs.precond: Successfully logged in with mobile 8888888888.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /sales-manager/callback-requests.
2. Read the greeting area.
tcs.expected: The greeting 'Welcome, Tester' is shown, derived from the user object returned by verify-otp.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP-sent success toast
tcs.description: Verify that the success toast appears after Send OTP and auto-dismisses.
tcs.precond: The mobile screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for '8888888888'.
2. Observe the toast.
tcs.expected: A top-center toast reads 'OTP sent successfully!' and auto-dismisses within the antd default timeout (rendered via message.useMessage + contextHolder).

tcs.scenario: To verify pasting an OTP fills all six boxes
tcs.description: Verify that pasting a complete 6-digit OTP auto-populates all six boxes.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown; the clipboard contains '258369'.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the first OTP box.
2. Paste (Ctrl+V).
tcs.expected: All six boxes auto-fill with one digit each, the Submit OTP becomes the focus target and no JavaScript error occurs.

tcs.scenario: To verify each OTP box accepts only one digit
tcs.description: Verify that each OTP box holds a single digit and overflow auto-advances to the next box.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Box 1.
2. Try typing '25'.
tcs.expected: '2' stays in Box 1 and '5' auto-advances into Box 2; no box holds more than one digit.

tcs.scenario: To verify Backspace on an empty OTP box steps back
tcs.description: Verify that pressing Backspace in an empty OTP box moves focus to the previous box and clears its digit.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown with '258' typed into boxes 1-3.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Box 4 (empty).
2. Press Backspace.
tcs.expected: Focus moves back to Box 3 and the '8' in Box 3 is cleared. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the backspace-step-back behaviour is implied by the segmented-box design but not stated in BRD/FRD; confirm.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP boxes reject non-numeric input
tcs.description: Verify that letters and special characters cannot be typed into the OTP boxes.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Box 1.
2. Try typing 'a', then '@', then '#'.
tcs.expected: No letters or symbols appear in any OTP box; only digits are accepted (otpRegex matches 6 digits). [VERIFY WITH DEV] field-level numeric restriction is implied by the digit-per-box design but not stated explicitly; confirm non-numeric is blocked.

tcs.scenario: To verify pasting a wrong-length value into the OTP boxes
tcs.description: Verify how the OTP boxes behave when a value of the wrong length is pasted into the first box.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Copy a wrong-length value (e.g. '2583' = 4 digits, then '25836912' = 8 digits).
2. Click Box 1.
3. Paste (Ctrl+V).
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] full-OTP paste is documented (SM_LGN_033) but wrong-length paste is not in BRD/FRD. [To verify] confirm a short paste fills only the available boxes and a long paste fills only the first six (excess ignored) with no error thrown.

tcs.scenario: To verify an incorrect OTP is rejected with an error
tcs.description: Verify that submitting a wrong OTP shows an error and keeps the user on the OTP screen.
tcs.precond: Send OTP is complete for a valid SM mobile and the OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter an incorrect 6-digit OTP (e.g. '000000').
2. Click Submit OTP.
3. Look at the error area.
tcs.expected: An error message is shown in the error area, no JWT is issued, the user stays on the OTP screen and the OTP boxes are cleared for re-entry.

tcs.scenario: To verify an invalid OTP clears the boxes and stays on screen
tcs.description: Verify that submitting an invalid OTP fails verification, clears the boxes and does not navigate.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown after sending OTP to 8888888888.
tcs.steps:
1. Type '000000' into the six OTP boxes.
2. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: Verification fails, an error message is shown (e.g. invalid OTP / 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'), the OTP boxes are cleared, no JWT is issued and there is no navigation to /sales-manager/callback-requests.

tcs.scenario: To verify a partial OTP blocks submission
tcs.description: Verify that a partial (less than 6-digit) OTP is blocked with a validation message.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Type '12345' (5 digits) into the OTP boxes.
2. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: A validation message 'OTP must be 6 digits' is shown; no verify API call is fired and the user stays on the OTP screen.

tcs.scenario: To verify an empty OTP blocks Submit
tcs.description: Verify that submitting with all OTP boxes empty triggers a required validation and fires no API call.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Leave the OTP boxes empty.
2. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: A validation message 'OTP is required' is shown and no verify API call is fired.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP input enforces 6 digits, numeric only
tcs.description: Verify that the OTP entry accepts only digits and only enables Submit at exactly 6 digits.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown after Send OTP.
tcs.steps:
1. Try typing letters in the OTP boxes.
2. Enter only 5 digits and click Submit.
3. Try entering 7 digits.
tcs.expected: The OTP entry accepts digits only and caps at 6; Submit stays blocked (or a validation message appears) until exactly 6 digits are entered.

tcs.scenario: To verify an expired OTP is rejected at Verify
tcs.description: Verify that submitting an OTP after the expiry window is rejected and the user is prompted to request a fresh one.
tcs.precond: Send OTP is complete and the configured OTP expiry window is known.
tcs.steps:
1. Receive a valid OTP.
2. Wait past the configured expiry window without verifying.
3. Enter the now-expired OTP.
4. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: The OTP is rejected as expired, no JWT is issued and the user is prompted to request a fresh OTP.

tcs.scenario: To verify an expired OTP resets to the mobile screen
tcs.description: Verify the client-side expiry path: an OTP entered after expiry is flagged via the expiry check and the view resets to Step 1.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen timer has reached 0 and the user enters the previously-issued OTP after the expiry window.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP.
2. Wait until the OTP expires (per otpExpires, checked client-side).
3. Enter the originally received OTP '258369'.
4. Submit.
tcs.expected: The client-side expiry check flags the OTP as expired; the error 'OTP has expired. Please request a new one.' is shown and the view resets to the mobile screen so the user must request a new OTP.

tcs.scenario: To verify a verify-otp 5xx surfaces a user-facing error
tcs.description: Verify that a server failure on verify-otp shows a friendly error and lets the user retry without reloading.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown; a 500 can be simulated on the verify endpoint.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter the OTP.
2. Force the verify-otp endpoint to return a 500 (block/throttle in DevTools).
3. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: A user-friendly error such as 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' is shown in the error area, any spinner clears and the user can retry without a page reload.

tcs.scenario: To verify repeated wrong OTPs never lock the account
tcs.description: Verify that unlimited wrong OTP attempts are rejected but never lock the account or rate-limit, and a later correct OTP still succeeds.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown for 8888888888.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit '111111'.
2. Submit '222222'.
3. Submit '333333'.
4. Submit several more random 6-digit OTPs.
5. Submit '258369'.
tcs.expected: Every wrong attempt is rejected with no lockout and no rate-limit, and the final correct OTP succeeds and logs in. (The 60s re-send gate is UI-only; no backend throttle is wired to the auth routes — security gap, see note 7.)

tcs.scenario: To verify Buyer-portal OTP is rejected on the SM portal
tcs.description: Verify portal OTP isolation — the Buyer OTP does not work on the SM portal.
tcs.precond: On the /sales-manager login page.
tcs.steps:
1. Type '8888888888' and select the 'Sales Manager Admin' role.
2. Click Send OTP.
3. Enter the Buyer-portal OTP '147258'.
4. Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: Verification fails (OTP is portal-specific), an error is shown, the OTP boxes are cleared, no JWT is issued and there is no navigation — the user stays on the OTP screen.

tcs.scenario: To verify Channel-Partner OTP is rejected on the SM portal
tcs.description: Verify portal OTP isolation — the Channel-Partner OTP does not work on the SM portal.
tcs.precond: On the /sales-manager login page.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for '8888888888' (role Sales Manager Admin).
2. Enter the CP-portal OTP '147258'.
3. Submit.
tcs.expected: Verify rejects the OTP, an error is shown, the boxes are cleared and login does not proceed — only the SM OTP '258369' succeeds (role isolation).

tcs.scenario: To verify an inactive SM is rejected at Send OTP
tcs.description: Verify that an SM account with Is Active = OFF is rejected at the send-otp step with the revoked message.
tcs.precond: An SM account exists with isActive = false. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an inactive SM mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter the inactive SM's mobile.
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: The backend returns 400 'Your access to the portal has been revoked' at send-otp; the OTP screen does NOT load. (FSD-correction: rejection happens at send-otp, not at verify.)

tcs.scenario: To verify an inactive SM is rejected even with a valid OTP
tcs.description: Verify that an inactive SM account cannot complete login even if a valid OTP is supplied.
tcs.precond: An SM account exists but is_active is false. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an inactive SM mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter the inactive SM's mobile.
2. Send OTP, enter a valid OTP and Submit.
tcs.expected: Login is rejected per FRD §1.5 Rule 4; an error message (account revoked / not active) is shown, no JWT is issued and there is no navigation. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm whether the block surfaces at send-otp (per SM_LGN_008) or at verify, and the exact inline string.

tcs.scenario: To verify a JWT is stored after successful verification
tcs.description: Verify that a JWT token is stored after a successful OTP verification and keeps the user logged in.
tcs.precond: UAT credentials 8888888888 / 258369; an active SM.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete the OTP login flow.
2. Open DevTools, Application, Storage.
3. Inspect localStorage.
tcs.expected: A JWT is stored (AUTH_TOKEN in localStorage); subsequent navigations carry the auth context and a reload keeps the user logged in until token expiry.

tcs.scenario: To verify localStorage keys are set on login
tcs.description: Verify that all four expected localStorage keys are present and populated after a successful login.
tcs.precond: About to perform a successful login.
tcs.steps:
1. Open DevTools, Application, localStorage.
2. Complete a successful login (8888888888 / 258369, role Sales Manager Admin).
3. Inspect localStorage.
tcs.expected: All four keys are present and populated: AUTH_TOKEN (JWT), user (serialized user object), permission_check (permissions blob) and persist:xanadu_0.0.1 (redux-persist root).

tcs.scenario: To verify stale tokens are cleared on entering the login route
tcs.description: Verify that entering /sales-manager wipes any stale auth tokens so the user is not auto-logged-in with a stale token.
tcs.precond: A stale AUTH_TOKEN is present in localStorage from a prior session.
tcs.steps:
1. With the stale token present, navigate to /sales-manager.
2. Inspect localStorage immediately after the route mounts.
tcs.expected: Stale auth-related keys are removed on login-route mount (Auth.clear()); the login form renders fresh and the user is not auto-logged-in with the stale token.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session persists across a page refresh
tcs.description: Verify that refreshing after login keeps the SM authenticated on the Callback Requests page.
tcs.precond: A successful login has completed; on /sales-manager/callback-requests.
tcs.steps:
1. Hard refresh the page (F5).
2. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: The page reloads, AUTH_TOKEN and persist:xanadu_0.0.1 persist, the user stays on /sales-manager/callback-requests (not redirected to login) and the dashboard renders with 'Welcome, Tester'.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session persists in a new tab
tcs.description: Verify that opening a protected SM URL in a new tab of the same browser does not prompt for login.
tcs.precond: The SM is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Open a new tab in the same browser.
2. Go to /sales-manager/callback-requests.
tcs.expected: The new tab loads the Callback Requests page directly without a login prompt (the JWT is shared via localStorage).

tcs.scenario: To verify the session survives a browser restart within the JWT window
tcs.description: Verify that closing and reopening the browser within the ~1-day window keeps the SM logged in.
tcs.precond: The SM is logged in and the JWT is stored in localStorage.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in successfully.
2. Close the browser completely.
3. Reopen the browser.
4. Go to /sales-manager/callback-requests.
tcs.expected: The session is restored from localStorage and the Callback Requests page loads without redirecting to login.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session lasts within the 1-day window
tcs.description: Verify that the session remains valid within the ~1-day JWT window.
tcs.precond: The SM is logged in and a JWT has been issued.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the login time.
2. Wait within the 1-day window (e.g. 23 hours).
3. Access a protected SM route.
tcs.expected: The session is still valid within the 24-hour window and the protected route loads without redirecting to login. [VERIFY WITH DEV] BRD states a session but does not state the exact JWT lifetime; confirm the ~1-day expiry for SM.

tcs.scenario: To verify behaviour at the JWT expiry boundary
tcs.description: Verify that the session is rejected at/after the JWT expiry and the user is sent to login.
tcs.precond: An aged/short-expiry SM JWT is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an aged/short-expiry token.
tcs.steps:
1. Use a JWT at/just past its expiry.
2. Access a protected SM route.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] BRD states the session lasts a configured window but the exact at-expiry behaviour and clock-skew tolerance are not documented. [To verify] confirm the request is rejected (401) and the user is redirected to /sales-manager at/after expiry.

tcs.scenario: To verify a second-device login does not invalidate the first
tcs.description: Verify that logging in on a second device leaves the first device's session intact (stateless JWT).
tcs.precond: The SM is logged in on Device A.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as the same SM on Device B.
2. Return to Device A.
3. Access /sales-manager/callback-requests.
tcs.expected: Both devices stay authenticated — the JWT is stateless and not bound to one device, and there is no session blacklist. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm there is no SM-side single-session enforcement.

tcs.scenario: To verify an unauthenticated protected route redirects to login
tcs.description: Verify that navigating to a protected SM route without a session redirects to the SM login.
tcs.precond: No SM session in the browser (localStorage cleared).
tcs.steps:
1. Open a browser without an SM JWT.
2. Navigate directly to /sales-manager/callback-requests.
3. Observe the redirect.
tcs.expected: The user is redirected to the /sales-manager login page; the protected target is not loaded and no protected data is exposed.

tcs.scenario: To verify the auth gate on direct deep-link access
tcs.description: Verify that a direct deep-link to a protected SM route in a fresh session redirects to login.
tcs.precond: localStorage is cleared / no AUTH_TOKEN.
tcs.steps:
1. Open a new incognito window.
2. Navigate directly to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/sales-manager/callback-requests.
tcs.expected: The app detects the missing JWT and redirects to /sales-manager (the login route); the SM login page renders and any stale state is cleared.

tcs.scenario: To verify a tampered JWT forces a redirect to login
tcs.description: Verify that editing the stored JWT causes the protected API call to fail and the user to be sent to login.
tcs.precond: The SM is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Open DevTools, Application, localStorage.
2. Change a character in the stored JWT.
3. Reload /sales-manager/callback-requests.
tcs.expected: The protected API call fails with 401 and the user is redirected to the /sales-manager login page.

tcs.scenario: To verify Back after login does not return to the login form
tcs.description: Verify that pressing the browser Back button after login does not show the OTP/mobile form again.
tcs.precond: Just completed SM login; on /sales-manager/callback-requests.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the browser Back button.
2. Observe the page state.
tcs.expected: The user remains in the authenticated app (stays on callback-requests or another protected route); the browser Back does not show the OTP/mobile login form again.

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout clears the session and redirects to login
tcs.description: Verify that logging out clears the client session and returns the user to the SM login page.
tcs.precond: The SM is logged in; on /sales-manager/callback-requests.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Logout in the user menu.
2. Observe the redirect.
3. Try navigating back to /sales-manager/callback-requests.
tcs.expected: The JWT is removed from storage, the user is redirected to the /sales-manager login page, and revisiting protected routes redirects back to login. (Note: this is a client-side clear — the JWT itself is NOT invalidated server-side; see SM_LGN_FSD_017.)

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout clears all auth keys and disconnects realtime
tcs.description: Verify that logout removes all four localStorage auth keys, disconnects the websocket and renders a fresh login form.
tcs.precond: Logged in as SM Admin on Callback Requests.
tcs.steps:
1. Trigger logout (via the header/menu logout control).
2. Observe the URL and localStorage.
tcs.expected: AUTH_TOKEN, user, permission_check and persist:xanadu_0.0.1 are removed from localStorage, the websocket is disconnected and the browser redirects to /sales-manager with a fresh empty login form.

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout does not invalidate the JWT server-side
tcs.description: Verify the documented security gap that the JWT stays usable after logout until natural expiry.
tcs.precond: The SM is logged in with an active JWT. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Capture the JWT bearer token.
2. Trigger logout (expect a client-side clear / 200).
3. Immediately call a protected SM endpoint with the same captured JWT.
tcs.expected: The logout clears the client session, but the captured JWT STILL succeeds on the protected endpoint — the token is stateless with no server-side blacklist, so it remains valid until its expiry (~1d). QA must NOT write a post-logout 401 pass case. (Security gap, shared with Admin auth.controller.)

tcs.scenario: To verify SQL injection in the mobile field is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that a SQL-injection string in the mobile field is blocked by the numeric-only input.
tcs.precond: The SM login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Try entering "' OR 1=1 --" in the mobile field.
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: The input is blocked at field level (numeric only); no DB error occurs and no login happens.

tcs.scenario: To verify XSS injection in the mobile field is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that a script payload in the mobile field is not executed.
tcs.precond: The SM login page is loaded.
tcs.steps: 1. Try entering '<script>alert(1)</script>' in the mobile field.
tcs.expected: The script tags are blocked by the numeric-only field; no JavaScript alert fires.

tcs.scenario: To verify auth requests are HTTPS only with no OTP in the URL
tcs.description: Verify that the login page and all auth requests use HTTPS and never carry mobile/OTP in the URL.
tcs.precond: DevTools is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Confirm the address bar shows https:// on /sales-manager.
2. Capture the send-otp and verify-otp requests in the Network tab.
3. Check the request method, URL and body.
tcs.expected: All auth requests are HTTPS; the mobile and OTP are sent in the request body, never in the URL/query; there are no mixed-content warnings and the auth payload is not logged to the console.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP is generated with insecure Math.random()
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that OTPs are generated with Math.random() rather than a CSPRNG (shared Admin/SM auth.controller).
tcs.precond: Source-review access or the ability to generate many OTPs. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] generation harness.
tcs.steps:
1. Trigger many OTP requests on UAT (script).
2. Analyse the distribution / predictability.
tcs.expected: OTP is generated via Math.floor(100000 + Math.random() * 900000) — NOT a CSPRNG. Document as a known security gap; recommend migrating to crypto.randomInt. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the SM path uses the same generator.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP is stored as plaintext
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that the OTP is persisted as plaintext on the users table.
tcs.precond: DB query access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] DB access.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for the SM user.
2. Query the users row for the otp and otpExpires columns.
tcs.expected: The otp column contains the literal 6-digit code in plaintext. Document the gap — it should be hashed (bcrypt or HMAC).

tcs.scenario: To verify the master OTP works in all environments
tcs.description: Verify the documented operational risk that the master OTP has no production gate.
tcs.precond: The master OTP is configured in the target environment. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] env access.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for any SM user.
2. Verify with the master OTP value (258369).
tcs.expected: Verify succeeds regardless of environment — there is NO production gate on the master OTP. Document the operational risk; confirm the master-OTP rotation policy with the security team. (SM/SM-Admin uses ADMIN_MASTER_OTP per SM_LGN_FSD_011.)

tcs.scenario: To verify OTP verification sends no notification
tcs.description: Verify that successfully verifying the OTP does NOT send any SMS, WhatsApp or email (silent by design).
tcs.precond: An SM successfully verifies the OTP. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] message-log visibility.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a successful OTP verification.
2. Check outbound message logs for SMS/WhatsApp/email tied to this verification.
tcs.expected: No SMS, WhatsApp or email is dispatched on OTP verification (silent by design). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm there is no side-channel notification on verify.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP is delivered via Epinet SMS (not Kaleyra)
tcs.description: Verify that the OTP SMS is dispatched through Epinet and NOT Kaleyra (FSD-correction 2026-05-25).
tcs.precond: Backend outbound network-log capture is available; a valid SM mobile. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] backend log access.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for 8888888888.
2. Inspect the backend's outbound HTTP traffic.
tcs.expected: The outbound OTP SMS hits the Epinet endpoint; there is NO Kaleyra call for the OTP. (Kaleyra is used only for WhatsApp/click-to-call to customers — BRD §7, FS 1.6.1.)

tcs.scenario: To verify send-otp is fire-and-forget (success even on dispatch failure)
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that send-otp returns success even when the outbound SMS dispatch fails.
tcs.precond: Backend with a simulated outbound failure to the SMS provider. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] network-fault injection.
tcs.steps:
1. Block outbound traffic to the Epinet endpoint.
2. Send OTP for the SM mobile.
tcs.expected: The backend returns 200 'OTP sent successfully' even though no message actually left the system, and the user row still has otp/otpExpires set (send calls are not awaited). Document the gap. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the SM path shares this fire-and-forget behaviour.

tcs.scenario: To verify a successful login is recorded in the audit log
tcs.description: Verify that a successful SM login is recorded with timestamp, mobile and role.
tcs.precond: An active SM logs in successfully. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] audit-log read access.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current timestamp.
2. Complete SM login with 8888888888 / 258369.
3. Query the audit log for the latest LOGIN event.
tcs.expected: An audit-log row exists with the SM's user ID, role (sales_manager or sales_manager_admin), mobile number and a timestamp within seconds of the login. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the audit-table/columns; FS §1.8 documents the requirement.

tcs.scenario: To verify a failed login is recorded in the audit log
tcs.description: Verify that a failed SM login attempt is recorded in the audit log.
tcs.precond: A valid SM mobile is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] audit-log read access.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for the valid SM mobile.
2. Enter a wrong OTP '000000'.
3. Click Submit OTP.
4. Query the audit log.
tcs.expected: A failed-login audit entry is recorded with the mobile, a timestamp and the failure reason (invalid OTP). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the failed-login audit is implemented per FS §1.8.

tcs.scenario: To verify the send-otp endpoint accepts a valid SM mobile (API)
tcs.description: Verify that the SM send-otp API returns success for a registered SM mobile.
tcs.precond: An API client / valid environment is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the SM send-otp endpoint with the SM mobile, countryCode '+91' and a role.
2. Read the HTTP status and response body.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with 'OTP sent successfully' (the response carries otpExpires). (Note: request field is `phone` with countryCode + role — see DOC_DRIFT-001.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the verify-otp endpoint returns a token and user (API)
tcs.description: Verify that the SM verify-otp API returns a JWT and user object for the correct mobile + OTP + role.
tcs.precond: An API client is available and send-otp has been called. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the SM verify-otp endpoint with the SM mobile, the master OTP, countryCode and role.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a JWT and a user object. (Note: token is returned wrapped as response.data.token — see DOC_DRIFT-001.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the permissions in the verify-otp response
tcs.description: Verify that a successful verify-otp response includes the permissions used to gate the SM UI.
tcs.precond: A successful SM OTP verification has been performed. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Perform a successful verify-otp for the SM mobile.
2. Inspect the response body for a permissions field.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the verify-otp response includes a permissions structure (Auth.permission = user.permissions per visual-memory). [To verify] confirm the exact module/action ids returned for the SM and SM-Admin roles.

tcs.scenario: To verify injection at the API layer bypasses the field block
tcs.description: Verify backend handling when a SQLi/XSS payload is sent directly to the SM send-otp API (bypassing the numeric-only field).
tcs.precond: An API client is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call send-otp with `phone` set to an injection payload.
2. Read the response and check for DB/error leakage.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the UI numeric-only block does not apply at the API. The backend should safely reject (parameterised queries; failing the user lookup with 400 'User not found') with no SQL error and no script reflection. [To verify] confirm backend sanitisation.

tcs.scenario: To verify the phone-format regex is not enforced backend
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that the phone-format check is commented out so any string passes format and fails only at user lookup.
tcs.precond: A UAT SM user with phone 8888888888 exists. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST send-otp with phone 'abc' and read the response.
2. POST send-otp with phone '12345' and read the response.
tcs.expected: The backend phone-format check is commented out, so it accepts any string and fails only on the user lookup, returning 400 'User not found'. Document the validation gap. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the SM path shares this commented-out validation.

tcs.scenario: To verify there is no backend OTP cooldown (API)
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that send-otp has no server-side rate limit — the 60s re-send gate is UI-only.
tcs.precond: An API client is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call send-otp for the SM mobile.
2. Immediately call send-otp again, back-to-back, several times.
tcs.expected: Every back-to-back send-otp call succeeds — there is NO server-side cooldown (the throttle is commented out at auth.controller.js:558-568). The 60s re-send gate exists only in the UI (FS 1.5 Rule 3). Document the gap; do not test backend cooldown as a passing case.

tcs.scenario: To verify Re-Send OTP is not backend-throttled (UI)
tcs.description: Verify from the UI that repeated Re-Send OTP after the timer expiry always succeeds (no backend throttle).
tcs.precond: On the OTP screen.
tcs.steps:
1. Wait for the countdown to expire.
2. Click Re-Send OTP.
3. Wait again and repeat three or more times.
tcs.expected: Each Re-Send after the timer expiry succeeds without backend throttling (FS 1.5 Rule 3 — cooldown commented out); a toast is shown each time and the UI timer restarts each cycle.

tcs.scenario: To verify hidden tracking fields on send-otp are tolerated
tcs.description: Verify that the send-otp endpoint silently accepts extra tracking fields without erroring (not a bug).
tcs.precond: An API client is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST send-otp for the SM mobile with extra fields (sessionId, utm_source, gclid, etc.).
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The endpoint accepts the request and returns success; the extra fields are ignored by the SM flow (tolerated by design). Do NOT flag the extra-field acceptance as a bug. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm no SM-side side effect.
